notes.lr-psa-application-document-withholding: A is clearly best, but the principle only restricts withholding ('may withhold only if'); it never requires withholding. So choice D (agency releases a document despite safety risk) does not technically violate the principle either. Consider rewording the principle to also require withholding when safety is endangered, or revise D so it is a withholding decision that fails the principle.
notes.lr-main-conclusion-downtown-parking-hous: D is the best answer, but the closing sentence ('Indeed, it is the businesses, far more than the council, that stand to gain') could be read by some test-takers as the main conclusion. C is kept wrong only by the overstatement 'more than anyone else' versus 'far more than the council.' Consider tightening so the final sentence reads unambiguously as support (e.g. 'In fact, ... stand to gain') or soften the wrong-answer trap.
notes.lr-parallel-method-bridge-collapse-cause: A is the best match (three options, two eliminated by evidence, third concluded). B is a tempting near-match but is hedged ('probably') and its elimination evidence is weaker; still defensible as the single answer. No change strictly needed.
